page: Amazon Web Services i8g.12xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by dedicated AWS Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz, delivering 48 physical cores across 48 vCPUs with a single thread per core architecture. The processor configuration includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache, backed by 384.0 GB of system memory, which establishes an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. The server comes equipped with 11,250 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 28 Gbps. It does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded performance and high I/O capability. The instance achieved top-tier rankings in Geekbench multi-core (24,079.0), software compilation with Clang (70,953.0), and PassMark database operations (47,385.11). Memory throughput is distinctly elevated, yielding 404.61 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 201.28 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth in top-tier tiers. Network and data delivery tests show strong results, including 102.83 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 98.01 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-threaded throughput falls in the middle range, as reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,885.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,706.9.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform delivers high compute, memory, and storage density within a single tenant boundary without hyperthreading contention. Because of its dedicated physical execution cores, generous memory allocation, massive local NVMe capacity, and high network bandwidth, this instance is suited for I/O-intensive database clusters, distributed search nodes, real-time analytics, and high-throughput static data serving.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.12xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized server instance based on the AWS Nitro system and Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. Featuring 48 dedicated physical cores with single-threading at 2.8 GHz, the system pairs 384.0 GB of memory with 11,250 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 28 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute, Clang compilation, memory bandwidth, and database operations, alongside 98.01 million Redis SET operations per second and 102.83 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-threaded metrics remain within average ranges. With no GPU hardware, its architectural tradeoffs favor high I/O density and sustained parallel throughput over burst or single-core instruction speeds, making it an effective choice for distributed databases, caching platforms, and storage-heavy data processing workloads.
